finding.claim: update_doc calls can_edit(g.user, doc) but discards the boolean result, so any caller with a set g.user can overwrite any document's body regardless of ownership or editor membership.
finding.source: PUT /doc/<doc_id> with JSON body; doc_id from URL path, body from request.json["body"]. Precondition: caller is authenticated so g.user is set (origin of g.user not in this directory), and knows or can guess doc_id.
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] at docs.py:20 (write to protected document content)

trace.note: Route registered for PUT /doc/<doc_id>, no decorator guard
doc = DOCS[doc_id] loads object by URL id with no owner/tenant check
can_edit(g.user, doc) evaluated but return value ignored; no abort/return/raise
Body written unconditionally to the document

finding.guards_checked: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) is logically correct but its result is unused at line 19. require_edit (docs.py:11-13) would abort(403) and is used correctly by update_title (line 27). No before_request or decorator in this file restricts update_doc. g.user is never set in this file, so route reachability beyond authentication is unverified. update_title is not affected: it uses require_edit and assigns only request.json["title"].

verdict.guard_found: none. The route at docs.py:16-18 has no decorator or before_request check. can_edit (docs.py:7-8) returns a bool, but the call at docs.py:19 is a bare statement whose result is discarded, so nothing aborts before the write at docs.py:20. require_edit (docs.py:11-13) is the guard that does abort(403), and update_doc does not call it. Its use in update_title (docs.py:27) is correct.
verdict.reason: The bare call to can_edit at docs.py:19 discards its boolean result, so the unconditional write at docs.py:20 runs for any caller, including one with no ownership or editor membership; the only abort in the file (docs.py:13 via require_edit) is never reached from update_doc. The attacker needs only to reach PUT /doc/<doc_id>, and any authentication enforced outside this file is unverified, but it would be a low-privilege authenticated user rather than an admin, so the finding stands.
